correctness.rationale: On finite height≤2 posets, every upset is specified by maximal trace S⊆M and independent decisions for each lower vertex v with N(v)⊆S. Consequently ¬U=P\↓S, all 2^m such R_S occur distinctly, and their fibers have counts f(S)=2^{Σ_{T⊆S,T≠∅}h(T)}. Since f(∅)=1, the normalized probability ratio p(S)/p(∅) gives the integer exponent c(S), whose unique Boolean Möbius inverse h(T) records every lower neighborhood count. Those counts completely reconstruct order up to maximal labels, and conversely nonnegative Möbius integers construct the unique suitable frame. Fast Boolean transform complexity O(m2^m) measured in indexed exact arithmetic operations. Independent direct enumeration of upsets, negations, fiber exponents and Möbius inversion over all labeled m≤3,l≤3 incidence frames matches the theorem; independent explicit examples have identical unordered histograms but distinct lower degrees. A three-chain has non-power-of-two boundary fiber (3), so scope is rightly confined to height two.
residual_risks: Probability law must retain Boolean identification of the output elements, not an unordered frequency multiset.
The exact arithmetic operation count ignores bit complexity for huge probabilities.
